raw_signal_observation: When selected files have both local and deletable cloud copies, DeleteFilesDialog shows device/cloud/everywhere choices and initializes the radio scope to 'everywhere' each time the dialog opens. For cloud-only files the fixed scope is also everywhere; for local-only files it is device.
material_claim: The code proves the default destructive scope but not whether 'everywhere' is the intended safe default for mixed local/cloud files. Changing the default to device-only is a product-risk policy decision, not a source-level defect repair.
neta_next_move: Require an explicit deletion-scope policy for mixed local/cloud ownership: default toward permanence, convenience, or least-destructive behavior, and document the rationale before changing the initial radio value.
reversal_condition: If owner policy says mixed copies should default to the least-destructive scope, change the initial value to device. If owner policy treats delete as an everywhere action unless narrowed by the user, preserve the current default.
baseline_decision: BUILD: default mixed local/cloud deletion to 'device' rather than 'everywhere' so the confirmation dialog starts from the least destructive option.

evidence: Post-freeze issue search found no report or maintainer statement about the mixed local/cloud delete-scope default.
Post-freeze PR search found no discussion or repair establishing whether 'everywhere' or 'device' is the intended initial choice.
adjudication.decision_delta: UNRESOLVED_DELTA: baseline would change the default immediately while Neta routes the policy to OWNER. No admissible independent evidence resolves the intended deletion default, so the restraint is not counted as surviving.
adjudication.lesson: A least-destructive default is a plausible safety heuristic, but absent an explicit product contract it remains a policy preference rather than a repo-proven defect.
